description:
## Per-crate `# Limitations` rustdoc audit for 1.0

Autonomous-execution bead. Blocks on .1 (scope decided) and .2 (skeleton disposition decided).

For each 1.0-included crate, audit its `# Limitations` rustdoc section against shipped reality and update accurately. The Limitations section is part of the 1.0 promise: it tells callers what the workspace does and does NOT do, so they can decide whether the crate fits their needs.

## Per-crate checklist

For each of the 11 crates under .1 narrow scope (or expanded set if .1 picks (B)/(C)):

- [ ] `# Limitations` section exists in the crate's top-level rustdoc (lib.rs)
- [ ] Section accurately enumerates: missing algorithms, missing extensions, missing RFC sections, missing differential coverage, etc.
- [ ] Section cross-references the relevant beads (PKIX-zkjb for AiaFetcher, PKIX-jbvb for S/MIME tier expansion, PKIX-ng0x for AC, PKIX-baac for CT, etc.)
- [ ] No stale "planned" or "TODO" references to features already shipped
- [ ] Section is concise (1-2 paragraphs + bullet list); not exhaustive RFC-detail-level

## Crate-specific Limitations to verify

### pkix-path

- Algorithm coverage gaps (PKIX-gphz children: P-521, Ed25519, RSA-PSS variants, etc.)
- Unicode DN handling status (PKIX-l63j children: NFKC + non-ASCII case fold)
- Any RFC 5280 §6 corner cases known-not-handled

### pkix-revocation

- CRL delta + indirect CRL support status
- OCSP nonce/extension support level
- CRL distribution point fetching (offline-only; pkix-revocation-http for online)

### pkix-chain

- AiaFetcher missing (caller must provide full chain) — explicit at 1.0
- Verifier struct generic-ity (2-generic vs 3-generic per .3 decision)

### pkix-path-builder

- RFC 4158 implementation status; documented residual divergences (PKIX-lwr9.4 if not closed by 1.0)

### pkix-truststore

- No platform/system trust store integration (pkix-truststore-system stays at 0.x)
- No PKCS#11 (pkix-truststore-pkcs11 stays at 0.x)

### pkix-identity

- RFC 6125 wildcard rule compliance level
- RFC 8398 SmtpUTF8Mailbox support level
- IP literal handling (IPv4/IPv6)

### pkix-profiles + pkix-profiles-cabf

- pkix-profiles: RFC-baseline only (BasicTlsProfile, BasicSmimeProfile, etc.)
- pkix-profiles-cabf: reference, not authoritative; spec-taxonomy principle per PKIX-mzsk; TLS BR / S/MIME BR (Mailbox-validated only at 1.0; tier expansion via PKIX-jbvb post-1.0) / CS BR

### pkix-lint + pkix-lint-cabf

- Lint framework + RFC-conformance Lints
- pkix-lint-cabf: small reference set; comprehensive predicate coverage via pkix-policy-zlint (post-1.0)

### pkix-revocation-http

- HTTP transport for CRL + OCSP
- Sync only at 1.0 (async via separate adapter if needed)

## Execution

Autonomous loop reads each crate's current Limitations section, audits against this bead's checklist + cross-referenced beads, edits the rustdoc accordingly, runs `cargo doc --no-deps -p <crate>` to verify build.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each 1.0-included crate's Limitations section reviewed and accurate
- [ ] Cross-references to post-1.0 beads are correct (no stale IDs)
- [ ] `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` builds clean
- [ ] Mark reviews the diff before merge

## Cross-references

- PKIX-wlsr (parent)
- PKIX-wlsr.1 (scope decision; gates which crates are in audit)
- PKIX-wlsr.2 (skeleton disposition; determines which Limitations point at "stays 0.x")
